previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of severe Crohn’s disease, status post subtotal colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis, was admitted for a flare characterized by severe left lower quadrant abdominal pain and frequent watery diarrhea—up to 40 episodes per day. He was initially kept NPO, started on IV fluids and IV steroids, and managed with pain control. Stool studies were negative for infectious causes. He gradually improved, tolerating a clear liquid diet and advancing to low-residue foods, with reduced pain and bowel frequency. He was transitioned to oral prednisone 60 mg daily and discharged home with instructions to follow up with his gastroenterologist for steroid tapering. His GERD was managed with omeprazole, and he was also discharged with loperamide, pain medication, and continued B12 injections.
problems: Regional enteritis of small intestine with large intestine

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST SINGLE VIEW, ___.

HISTORY:  ___ male with Crohn's flare and left lower quadrant
tenderness.  Question free air.

FINDINGS:  PA view of the chest is compared to previous exam from ___.  The lungs are clear.  There is no large effusion.  Cardiomediastinal
silhouette is normal.  The osseous and soft tissue structures are
unremarkable.  No free air identified below the diaphragm.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.  No free air below the
diaphragm.

INDICATION:  ___ man with Crohn's disease, question bowel movement
changes, left lower quadrant abdominal pain, and lower back pain, assess for
nephrolithiasis, small bowel obstruction, or ileus.

COMPARISONS:  MR enterography from ___ and CT abdomen and pelvis
with contrast from ___.

FINDINGS:  Three views of the abdomen were provided.  There is no evidence of
obstruction, ileus, or free air.  Dilated loop of neoterminal ileum in the
pelvis measures 5 cm and is a chronic finding.  There are no new abnormally
dilated bowel loops identified.  The visualized osseous structures are
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  Known dilated loop of neoterminal ileum in the pelvis is chronic.
No evidence of new obstruction or free air.

INDICATION:  ___ man with severe Crohn's disease presenting with
increased bowel motions and left abdominal and lower back pain.  Please
evaluate for Crohn's complications.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to previous MRI studies and CT studies, most
recently dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T2-weighted imaging obtained with a 1.5 Tesla magnet. 
Dynamic imaging was performed prior to, during, and following the uneventful
intravenous administration of 0.1 mmol/kg (8mL) of Gadovist.  In addition, 900
mL of oral VoLumen was administered to mark the bowel contents.  In addition,
1 mg of IM glucagon was administered to reduce bowel motion.

FINDINGS:  There is mild dilation of multiple small bowel loops with loops of
jejunum measuring 2.5 cm (6:10).  The patient is status post colectomy with
ileorectal anastomosis.  The region of the anastomosis appears intact.  There
is a persistent segment of abnormal mucosal enhancement, mural edema and
thickening and mesenteric hyperemia involving an ileal loop proximal to the
anastomosis.  This measures 6cm in length (1002:47) and is unchanged in
appearance from previous CT of ___.  There is proximal dilation of an
ileal loop measuring 4.6cm, which was also dilated previously present.  There
is a new area of abnormal bowel mucosa proximal to the dilated ileal loop
(1001:21) with mucosal hyperenhancement, mesenteric hyperemia and mural
thickening consistent with a skip lesion.
Within the right upper quadrant, a loop of mildly enhancing bowel represents
collapsed bowel in this region with no evidence of abnormality (1001:57).
No other skip lesions are identified.

The visualized portions of the liver are normal in appearance.  The spleen is
normal in size.  The pancreas, both adrenal glands are normal.  Both kidneys
enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically.  There are bilateral subcentimeter
renal cysts.
No free fluid

MR PELVIS:  The urinary bladder, prostate, anus and rectum are normal in
appearance.  There is no free fluid.  There are stable bone islands within the
right iliac crest.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Evidence of acute on chronic Crohn's disease involving the distal ileum
proximal to the ileorectal anastomosis with mucosal hyperenhancement,
mesenteric hyperemia and mural thickening.
2.  A new skip lesion is identified just proximal to a loop of dilated distal
ileum within the right lower quadrant which also demonstrates mucosal
hyperenhancement, mural thickening, and adjacent hyperemia. The remainder of
the small bowel is mildly dilated. No abscess or fistula identified.
3.  Bilateral subcentimeter renal cysts.

INDICATION:  Crohn's disease on chronic prednisone.  Left back and abdominal. 
Evaluate for epidural abscess.

COMPARISONS:  MRI of the L-spine, ___.  CT of the abdomen and
pelvis, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Routine enhanced MRI of the lumbar spine was obtained, including
sagittal and axial T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and STIR images.   7 mL of
Gadovist contrast was administered and post-contrast images were obtained.

FINDINGS:  
The vertebral body heights are preserved.  There is normal alignment.  The
bone marrow signal is unremarkable.  There is no evidence of osteomyelitis or
discitis.  No fractures are identified. 

Multilevel degenerative changes are stable from the prior exam.  The levels of
L1-2, L2-3, and L3-4 are unremarkable without significant degenerative
changes.  

At L4-5, there is a small disc bulge and facet arthropathy which is unchanged
from the prior exam.  There is no significant spinal canal or neural foraminal
narrowing.  

At L5-S1, there is an asymmetric disc bulge, slightly larger on the left than
the right, which is causing mild right and moderate left neural foraminal
narrowing.  This is also unchanged from prior exam.

The spinal cord signal is normal.  There are no enhancing lesions or fluid
collections within the spinal canal to suggest epidural abscesses or
hematomas.  The soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of epidural abscess.
2.  Stable degenerative changes as described above.

INDICATION:  Crohn's disease on high-dose steroids, left-sided back and hip
pain, pain on external rotation and abduction of the hip, evaluate for AVN of
the hip.

COMPARISON:  MRI of the hips on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MRI of the hips without contrast.  Coronal T1 and coronal STIR and
axial T2 fat sat images were obtained.

FINDINGS:  Images are directed toward evaluation of the hip joints.  There is
no fracture or dislocation involving either hip.  No significant degenerative
changes are identified.  There is no bone marrow edema.  There is no joint
effusion.  There is no evidence of avascular necrosis.  

The visualized portions of muscles and soft tissues about the pelvic girdle
are within normal limits in signal intensity and morphology.  There is no
edema identified about the greater trochanter to suggest trochanteric
bursitis.  The piriformis muscles are symmetric.  There is evidence of L5/S1
disc desiccation.  The SI joints are unremarkable.  The examination of the
pelvic parenchymal structures is limited but grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of avascular necrosis or fracture.

2.  L5/S1 degenerative disc disease.
